text:
ezra: heads-up — our preflight SAST job in the monorepo started spamming alerts after the weekend IAM tidy. suppression fetch failed and CI showed no KMS audit entries for the runner SA. tagging @mina @kai, short thread.

mina: on it. quick read: the suppression file is served from gs://sec-suppress and the fetch step got a 403. runner logs: 
```
2026-10-05T02:07:11Z fetcher: GET https://storage.googleapis.com/sec-suppress/suppressions.json 403
2026-10-05T02:07:12Z scanner: open /tmp/artifacts/abcd: permission denied
```

kai: interesting bit: infra-ops added a conditional binding on the KMS key yesterday (CR-2026-10-04) that limits access by request.time < "2026-10-04T00:00:00Z" for some migration window. if the same tidy removed a group binding used by the CI SA, that could explain both missing KMS logs and the suppression fetch issue if suppressions are encrypted.

ezra: we encrypt suppressions with KMS and the runner unwraps them at runtime. can you confirm whether the file is encrypted?

mina: yes, there's a small wrapper service that calls KMS.decrypt to unwrap the signed suppressions blob. wrapper logs show: 
```
2026-10-05T02:06:58Z unwrap: KMS decrypt failed: PermissionDenied: projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/scan-suppress-v3: condition prevents access
```

kai: that "condition prevents access" ties back to the time-based IAM condition. CR notes say the condition should only apply to the ops-group, but someone accidentally applied it to the whole binding set. infra-admin, can you pull the key IAM?

infra-admin: pulling now. IAM binding excerpt: 
- member: serviceAccount:ci-preflight@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
  condition: { title: "migration-window", expression: "request.time < timestamp('2026-10-04T00:00:00Z')" }
This was incorrectly applied to the binding for the CI SA.

dev-bot: created ticket SEC-5120 "preflight KMS conditional-binding rollback + audit" and tagged infra-ops.

ezra: mitigation plan: 1) remove condition on the CI SA binding (or re-add unconditioned short-lived grant), 2) re-run preflight, 3) verify KMS audit shows decrypt by ci-preflight at run time, 4) add preflight check to GH job that fails fast if decrypt or fetch fail.

mina: i can apply an ephemeral unconditioned grant (30m) now. command: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/PRJ/locations/global/keyR/keys/scan-suppress-v3 \\ 
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-preflight@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com \\ 
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

kai: after ephemeral grant, confirm wrapper logs show decrypt and that suppression signature verification passes. also check logs for the signed payload verification (we verify GPG signature on the suppressions blob).

infra-admin: ephemeral grant applied at 02:14 UTC.

logbot: KMS audit entry: Decrypt by principalPayload=serviceAccount:ci-preflight@prj.iam.gserviceaccount.com at 2026-10-05T02:14:31Z

mina: re-run results: suppression fetch succeeded and signature verification passed. SAST noise dropped 63 -> 7 (real findings).

kai: next steps (short): 1) INFRA: rollback the condition on the CI SA binding or scope it correctly to ops-group ONLY; 2) DEVSEC: add GH preflight step that validates KMS decrypt + blob signature before running scanner; 3) DOC: add a short note in the RBAC playbook about conditional IAM hazards; 4) long-term: store repo-level fallback suppressions signed in-tree so builds don't depend on a single external SA.

ezra: agreed. assigning: infra-admin -> SEC-5120 (fix binding + audit), mina -> SEC-5121 (GH preflight PR + signature check), kai -> SEC-5122 (playbook blameless note).

infra-admin: will attach IAM diff and audit evidence to SEC-5120.

mina: opening PR for preflight, will include a small script to gcloud kms decrypt a test blob and verify GPG sig.

ezra: thanks all :thumbsup: closing once PR and INFRA ticket reference are added to SEC-5120.
